  "final_quality": "tie",
  "reason": "Both support the same consequential outcome: independent local validation and preview can proceed, while integration requires an owner-supplied approved sandbox and verified service contract. Both retain atomic publication, unrelated-SKU preservation, idempotent retry, live failure/interruption/recovery acceptance and baseline preservation. Neither claims that offline failures, planned tests or structural checks establish service readiness. The differences in detail and review rework do not demonstrate superior final quality.",
  "decisive_evidence": [
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "No offline exception or local simulation qualifies.",
      "locator": "plans[0].final.work_items[W3].context",
      "consequence": "The unavailable service contract remains unresolved; local evidence cannot satisfy external readiness."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "Future owner supplies SERVICE-READY-1 approved sandbox, authoritative contract and actual supported readiness probes; unsupported capability blocks W4 rather than relaxing guarantees.",
      "locator": "plans[0].final.assumptions[A4].settle",
      "consequence": "Integration has an owned, substantive prerequisite and cannot proceed by weakening the requested guarantees."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Ready: W1 validator and test_TC_V01–V03 evidence accepted; service readiness is not required.",
      "locator": "plans[0].final.work_items[W2].context",
      "consequence": "Local preview remains eligible after local validation, independently of the unavailable sandbox."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "W1 parser -> W2 safe CLI can proceed independently of externally supplied W3 SERVICE-READY-1;",
      "locator": "plans[0].final.summary",
      "consequence": "The same useful local work remains available without inventing remote authority."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "After integration, S01–S04 remain due on the actual command and approved service, including success, partial failure, interrupted publication and recovery.",
      "locator": "planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/environment.md, External prerequisite INV-SERVICE-READY",
      "consequence": "Readiness evidence does not replace subsequent implementation acceptance at the real boundary."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "Execute TC06–TC09 and concurrency/permission branches at approved real boundary with independent status/inventory/audit evidence; never accept local simulation.",
      "locator": "plans[0].final.assumptions[A5].settle",
      "consequence": "Publication, retry and recovery remain future live obligations rather than inferred local successes."
    }
  ],
  "initial_plan_and_rework": "Both initial plans already established W1 → W2, independent external W3, and W2 + W3 → W4. A's review explicitly separated future sandbox execution from general activation, reducing a meaningful gate ambiguity; its initial W4 already included an approved opt-in live-test route, so a definite original deadlock is not established. B added an exact parser-only W1 confirmation command, removing ambiguity caused by the documented combined parser/CLI route. B also corrected experiment-allowance accounting and narrowed overlapping assumption ownership. These are useful bounded repairs, not new service evidence. B's earlier test-strategy readiness/acceptance correction preceded its initial plan and should be counted separately from Plan Improve rework.",
  "earlier_evidence_value": "The request and inspected transport source already establish that the deliberate pre-request failure cannot distinguish service contracts. Actual baseline executions establish only local runner availability and existing exception behavior. Reusing those observations while source, tests and runtime remain unchanged is valid. Earlier strategy work already supplied the local/live separation and future acceptance procedures. Neither side needed an experiment to rediscover the offline limitation, and neither incorrectly treated provisional schema choices as empirically verified service facts.",
  "harms_or_lost_requirements": [],
  "individual_judgment_corrections": [
    "No clear factual error is demonstrated in either judgment's core N1–N5 conclusions. Both correctly distinguish observed baseline behavior, implementation acceptance still due and unavailable external readiness.",
    "A's statement that no dependency demonstrably changed needs qualification: graph edges stayed fixed, but final W4 explicitly distinguished sandbox-test authority from general activation. This has practical clarification value, although the initial opt-in route limits any claim that review rescued an otherwise impossible plan.",
    "B's parser-only correction improves the specified confirmation route; initial W1 already intended independent parser verification. It does not demonstrate a superior final architecture or a newly discovered service capability.",
    "The alleged redundant commands or reads are cost observations, not demonstrated regressions. B's duplicate-read allegation cannot be independently confirmed from this paired record."
  ],
  "confidence": "high",
  "limits": [
    "Neither plan implements or verifies the new command. The observed passing suite covers one existing offline-transport test; planning completion is not feature acceptance.",
    "Approved service access, contract guarantees, fault facilities and actual live outcomes remain unavailable. Both plans correctly remain conditional.",
    "B's alleged duplicate reads at events 13/17 and the exact original allowance statement at event 127 require omitted raw evidence or the original note for independent verification. Retained review notes corroborate the accounting correction, but not every event-level allegation.",
    "A rejects empty batches while B permits an empty preview. Both present this as a provisional local default, and the request specifies no empty-batch policy; this difference does not establish a lost requirement."
  ]
}
